title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity: Sparsity: and At

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction claims: 'We find that: (i) applying key layer gating (G3) yields superior performance improvements compared to SDPA or value gating, reducing PPL by up to 0.3 and improving MMLU significantly.' The abstract states the central finding is an SDPA-gate improvement, and Table 1 (Section 3.2.1) shows SDPA gating (G1) achieves PPL 5.761 while key gating (G3) PPL is 6.016, proving G1 is clearly better than G3. The introduction's assertion contradicts the main experimental evidence and the abstract's conclusion.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 1 middle table and its caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The middle table in Figure 1 shows PPL for 15B MoE models: baseline 6.05, SDPA 5.95, key 5.75, etc., where key (G3) achieves the lowest PPL. Yet the figure caption explicitly states: 'Gating after SDPA (G1) yields the best overall results.' This directly contradicts the numerical values presented in the figure's own table.

Figure 3 displays gating score distributions for SDPA elementwise (left), value elementwise (middle), and head-shared (right). The caption claims: 'The majority of gating scores fall mostly between 0.4 and 0.7, indicating less sparsity.' However, Table 4 reports the mean gating score for SDPA elementwise gating as 0.116; a distribution with mean 0.116 cannot have the majority of values between 0.4 and 0.7. The caption incorrectly characterizes the left panel.

Reference [71] is given as 'OpenAI. GPT-OSS-120B & GPT-OSS-20B Model Card, 2025.' There is no publicly known GPT-OSS model from OpenAI, and this reference appears to be fabricated. A careful reviewer would demand verification or removal.

The paper states: '...and the unseen GatorNet [82] architecture provide critical foundations...' The reference list contains only entries up to [71]. Citation [82] is entirely missing from the bibliography, making the reference invalid.

The paper cites 'Rahul Dey and Fathi M. Salem. Gate-variants of gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural networks. MWSCAS, 2017' as the origin of GRUs. The original GRU was introduced by Cho et al. (2014); the 2017 paper discusses variants. This misattributes the primary source of the GRU architecture.

The title reads 'Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity: Sparsity: and At', which is truncated and ungrammatical. The intended complete title (as given in the abstract) is 'Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free'. This is a clear presentational error.
